# Bhikkhāparamparajātaka (Ja 496)

**ID:** Ja 496  
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhāparamparajātaka  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul13.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul13.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Bhikkhāparamparajātaka* (Ja 496) is a canonical birth story in the Jātaka collection, positioned at the conclusion of the *Pakiṇṇakavagga* in the fourth volume of Fausböll's edition [Fausböll 1887]. According to its opening narrative framework, the Buddha related this discourse while residing at Jetavana concerning a faithful and devoted landowner (*kuṭumbika*) who continually offered hospitality and honor to the Buddha and the Saṅgha [Fausböll 1887]. Modern scholarship highlights that the narrative sharply differentiates the *paccekabuddha* from the traditional Brahmanic ascetic (*tāpasa*), designed to demonstrate that among all social and religious dignitaries, the Buddhist monastic—embodied in the story by the *paccekabuddha*—is the preeminent recipient worthy of alms (*dakkhiṇeyya*) [Wiltshire 1990]. In the concluding identification of the birth story (*samodhāna*), the landowner is identified with the contemporary devotee, while past figures are linked to Ānanda (the king), Sāriputta (the royal priest), and the Bodhisatta (the Himalayan ascetic) [Fausböll 1887].

**Sources**

- [Fausböll 1887] V. Fausböll, Jataka Together with Its Commentary, Vol. 4 (1887) — Attested the text's placement in the Pakiṇṇakavagga, opening nidāna framing, and samodhāna identifications.
- [Wiltshire 1990] Martin G. Wiltshire, Ascetic Figures before and in Early Buddhism (1990) — Described the text's purpose regarding dakkhiṇeyya and the distinction between the tāpasa and the paccekabuddha.
